t: Swahili grew from the Bantu speech of the East African coast, where from around the 8th century merchant towns traded across the Indian Ocean with Arabia, Persia and India, absorbing many Arabic words.

Written in Arabic script from at least the early 18th century, it developed a rich poetic tradition, and in the 19th century caravans carried it inland from Zanzibar as far as the Great Lakes and the Congo.

Spread by colonial administrations and, after independence, promoted by Tanzania as its national language, it is today the common language of East Africa and one of the most widely spoken languages of the continent.
dyk: Julius Nyerere, the first president of Tanzania, translated Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar and The Merchant of Venice into Swahili, to show that the language could carry any literature in the world.
ev: Trading towns such as Shanga and Manda grow on the East African coast, where Swahili takes shape
Ibn Battuta visits Mombasa and Kilwa and describes the wealth of the Swahili coast
Letters in Arabic script written at Kilwa, later seized by the Portuguese and kept at Goa, are the oldest known documents in Swahili
The Utendi wa Tambuka, the oldest dated epic poem in Swahili, is composed
Caravans from Zanzibar carry Swahili to the Great Lakes and the eastern Congo
A committee of the British East African territories standardises Swahili on the dialect of Zanzibar
Tanzania makes Swahili the language of government and of primary schooling
The first World Kiswahili Language Day is celebrated on 7 July, proclaimed by UNESCO

f.family: Niger-Congo: a Bantu language of the Sabaki group, with many words borrowed from Arabic
f.script: The Arabic script from at least the early 18th century; the Latin alphabet since the 19th century
f.earliest: Letters written at Kilwa in 1711 and the epic poem Utendi wa Tambuka of 1728, in Arabic script
f.status: Spoken by well over 100 million people, most of them as a second language; official in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and Rwanda and a working language of the African Union
